sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Remote Desktop Access and Unattended Machine Telemetry Software

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Double Taxation Agreement and Investment Protection Agreement
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L. 561-1 et seq. and L. 561-45 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) as amended by the transposition of the 5th AML Directive; Article L. 561-2-2 of the same Code creating the beneficial ownership register; Décret n° 2017-1094 du 6 juin 2017 on the beneficial ownership register; Règlement Général de l'Autorité des Marchés Financiers (AMF) for listed entities; ACPR instructions on AML/CFT.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the ultimate beneficial owner's valid passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent law enforcement, notary, or consulate of the holder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of the UBO (utility bill, bank statement, or tax notice)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local utility provider, bank, or tax authority in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in France or notary/consulate in the appointer's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft articles of association (statuts constitutifs) bearing French notarial certification if capital in-kind
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French notary or registered business formation professional
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No external legalization if established in France; foreign-language annexes require apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against the French national FICOV (Tracfin) lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List (for USD transactions or U.S.-connected parties), and the intergovernmental FATF high-risk and non-cooperative jurisdictions list; enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs based on the FATF definition; negative news and adverse media checks are governed by Article L. 561-10-1 of the Code monétaire et financier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in French or in Latin characters; any non-Latin script must be transliterated. French-language names must comply with French orthographic and typographic conventions, and the name must not contain words or expressions contrary to French public policy or to public morality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the Registre National des Entreprises, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal through the Guichet unique portal within 30 days of the refusal, stating the legal grounds and providing additional evidence of distinctive character or non-confusion. If the administrative appeal is dismissed, the applicant may bring summary proceedings before the competent Tribunal judiciaire (litige de la formation) for judicial review within two months. Alternatively, the applicant may file a revised name application avoiding the conflicting elements to preserve time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Fully permissible for a remote desktop access and telemetry software company; the SAS may use a registered business address (domiciliation) provided by an approved business center or intermediary, subject to a genuine administrative and management presence, and must accept service of process at that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% annualized probability for low-risk software entities, subject to increase if tax inconsistencies, UBO reporting failures, or unusual transaction patterns are detected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization fees for personal identification documents of each UBO/shareholder
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (France) or the competent apostille authority of the document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for apostille; prevailing consular fee for non-Hague countries

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and legal review of French SAS articles of association (statuts) by a licensed French avocat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a standard single-member or multi-member SAS incorporating a software activity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the mandatory incorporation legal notice (avis de constitution) in a French Journal d'annonces légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory capped tariff for corporate legal announcements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing fee for the incorporation dossier through the Guichet unique and registration with the Registre National des Entreprises
Nominal registration duties and Chamber of Commercial Taxes (taxe pour frais de chambre de commerce) applicable to an SAS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Administration fiscale and local Chamber of Commerce (CCI)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce): Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10 (general company provisions), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-29 (Société par Actions Simplifiée), Articles L. 123-1 to L. 123-33 (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés), and Articles R. 224-1 et seq. (registration procedure and filing formalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités (single electronic filing window); downstream judicial control and registration by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office, which maintains the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company incorporation dossier filed as Form M0 (Demande d'immatriculation au RCS) together with the signed Articles of Association, filed electronically via the INPI Guichet Unique portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum share capital is required for an SAS (capital may lawfully be €1 or any higher amount). If capital is fixed, cash contributions must be paid up to at least 50% at incorporation, with the balance payable within five years. The paid-up portion must be deposited to a blocked escrow account maintained with a French bank, the Caisse des Dépôts, or a notary, and may be released only after the delivery of the Kbis registration extract. Contributions in kind must be fully transferred at incorporation and reported in the Articles of Association. No statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is required unless statutory turnover/balance-sheet/workforce thresholds are exceeded or the bylaws so provide.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — FR_SAS. Whereas the share capital has been fully subscribed, the subscribers hereby resolve: (1) the subscription of all issued shares is ratified; each founder acknowledges payment of at least 50% of cash contributions into the blocked escrow account held with the depositary bank, with the unpaid balance callable at any time within five years; (2) the draft Articles of Association are adopted without reservation and constitute the corporation; (3) the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Articles, and the President is authorised to conclude the occupancy contract; (4) the President appointed this day is vested with full powers to complete the registration before the INPI and the RCS, open bank accounts, and employ personnel. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles of Association and Beneficial Owner Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders and President acting under private signature; public notary mandatory only if real property is contributed; ultimate filing authority is the INPI Guichet Unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association in French, indicating corporate form (SAS), share capital, share allocation, registered office, duration, corporate object focused on remote desktop access and IoT telemetry software, and appointment of the President. Have all shareholders individually sign each page and the final signature page with timestamp. Prepare the official beneficial owner declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) identifying any natural person holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights or exercising control. If the President signs the Articles, attach a copy of their identity document and the non-disqualification declaration (attestation de non-condamnation).
required_dossiers: French-language Articles of Association (statuts constitutifs)
Share subscription and capital allocation schedule
Declaration of Beneficial Owner (RBE)
Identity document of the President and certificate of non-disqualification
Consent to appointment signed by the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique or the Greffe identifies a legal insufficiency in the Articles or the RBE, execute a rectifying addendum, refile the RBE, and resubmit the complete package within the procedural cure period granted by the Greffe (typically 15 days from the query).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Share Capital into Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or notary acting as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing the incorporation dossier, collect the cash portion of share capital and deposit at least 50% thereof into a temporarily blocked account opened in the name of the company 'en formation' or in the name of the subscribers acting for the future company. Instruct the depositary to issue a signed certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) expressly stating that the funds are blocked and will be released only upon presentation of the Kbis. Retain the certificate for attachment to the M0 filing.
required_dossiers: Signed deposit certificate issued by the bank or notary
Proof of transfer or remittance of the subscribed cash portion
Company formation project statement prepared for the depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account for an unregistered company, execute the subscription act through a notary escrow deposit or use a bank branch accepting 'compte bloqué pour constitution'. Where the certificate is defective, obtain a corrected statement before submitting the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Newspaper authorized to receive legal announcements (Journal d'Annonces Légales, JAL) in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a mandatory incorporation notice in an authorized legal gazette, stating the corporate name, form (SAS), share capital, registered office address, number of shares, corporate object, the President's name, and the planned RCS registration city. File the notice at least one day before or on the day of submission of the incorporation dossier, pay the publisher's fee, and obtain the attestation de parution with the publication date and exact wording.
required_dossiers: Notice wording signed by a founder
Copy of the Articles of Association used by the JAL
Attestation de parution issued by the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication record is lost or contains an error, cause the JAL to issue a corrected attestation or republish a corrective notice; the attestation must be re-uploaded to the Guichet Unique before the registry closes the file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Incorporation Dossier at the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités (online portal); thereafter transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the guichedit unique portal (guichetunique.inpi.fr), select 'immatriculation d'une personne morale', complete the M0 form with corporate, officer, registered office, capital, and activity data, upload the Articles of Association, attestation de parution, capital deposit certificate, RBE, and proof of occupancy of the registered office. Certify the declaration by electronic signature of the President, pay the applicable registration taxes and fees, and retain the acknowledgment of receipt with the registration reference.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed M0 form
Articles of Association (PDF)
Attestation de parution from the JAL
Capital deposit certificate
Declaration of Beneficial Owner
Proof of occupation of the registered office (lease, sublease, or domiciliation contract)
Payment receipt of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a request for regularization or evidence, read the query through the Guichet Unique, supply the missing document or correction within the granted period (normally 15 days), pay any supplemental fee if required, and await resumption of the registration process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Judicial Verification and Registration at the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique du Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registrar of the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the initial filing is transmitted, the Greffier verifies compliance of the statutory formalities, the capacity of the President, the legality of the corporate object, and the accuracy of the published notice. Upon satisfaction, the company is registered and assigned a SIREN number; the Greffe issues the definitive Kbis extract (existence légale certificate), which is the conclusive proof of legal incorporation and provides the SIRET for the registered office.
required_dossiers: Complete M0 file electronically transmitted by the Guichet Unique
Validated identity and non-disqualification evidence for the President
Attestation of publication conforming to legal requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe refuses registration, request a written reasoned decision, remedy the notified defect, or appeal the refusal before the jurisdictional court (Tribunal de Commerce) within 15 days of notification; alternatively, refile a cleaned dossier through the Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social, and Operational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFiP (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques), URSSAF, CNAV, and optional CNIL for data protection compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS registration automatically transmits the company's identification to the DGFiP and the social administration; however, confirm that the company is assigned its tax account and that the President has received the temporary tax identification number and the social security affiliation. Open an operational business bank account. If the software activity processes personal data in connection with remote screen sharing or IoT telemetry, file a GDPR formalities mitigation or appoint a Data Protection Officer as applicable. Also subscribe to professional liability insurance and, where applicable, register for the EU One Stop Shop or use Stripe/Paddle as payment facilitators for the collection of VAT on digital services.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
President's identity and residence address
Business bank account opening documents
Professional insurance certificate
GDPR compliance documentation (data mapping, privacy notice, DPO appointment if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax reference is missing, contact the local company tax service (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) within eight days with a copy of the Kbis to obtain the tax number. If the social affiliation is delayed, URSSAF may be alerted directly by the President. In case of GDPR deficiency, suspend telemetry data collection until a lawful basis and privacy documentation are fully in place.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None for ISIC 6201 software publishing and remote access services; coordinate with the Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE) for digital policy matters and with the CNIL for personal data in screen-sharing and IoT telemetry processing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or professional operating permit is required for remote desktop support and telemetry software. The legal operability proof is the Kbis extract; for regulated sectors involving critical infrastructure or health data, a sectoral authorization may be assessed as a fact-based case, but none is mandated for the ordinary SaaS commercial model.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale et interdépartementale de l'Environnement (DRIEAT) / Ministère de la Transition Écologique et de la Cohésion des Territoires
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is a non-classified service activity and does not fall under the nomenclature of Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) or the EIA categories applicable to industrial facilities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC thresholds applicable; office-based operations must comply with general municipal waste rules, with IT equipment and electronic waste (WEEE) handled through certified recyclers under Extended Producer Responsibility obligations, and with General Data Protection Regulation principles governing telemetry data as the sole environmental-adjacent compliance area.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any physical office and registered premises, obtain a fire safety classification and, where occupancy thresholds apply, a fire commission certificate for the premises (ERP class or simple office declaration). There is no mandatory civil defense clearance for software activity. The employer must carry out a single risk assessment document (Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels, DUERP) covering working-from-home, screen use, and electrical equipment, and register the staff health file; if more than 50 employees, establish the social and economic committee (CSE) and follow the occupational health and safety procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) of the French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; online portal: impots.gouv.fr (professional e-service 'Gérer mon entreprise'). Customs and indirect taxes are jointly administered by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI); customs portal: douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the SAS through the Guichet Unique des formalités des entreprises, transmitting the company statutes and declaration of the beneficial owner. Step 2 — Obtain from INSEE the SIREN and SIRET numbers and complete the enterprise register. Step 3 — Declare the start of the taxable activity; DGFiP automatically attributes the French intra-Community VAT number (n° TVA intracommunautaire) linked to the SIRET. Step 4 — Register for the DGFiP electronic filing service (impots.gouv.fr) for VAT returns (Form CA3) and corporate income tax returns. For a non-resident entity carrying out taxable supplies in France without a French establishment, file Form 3916-sd with the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises to obtain a French VAT number; a tax representative may be required under Article 289 A of the French General Tax Code where the taxable person is not established in the EU and no VAT identification has been obtained in France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box system. An SAS is by default a French corporate income taxpayer (impôt sur les sociétés) and cannot elect pass-through treatment. The only transparency option under Article 239 bis AB of the French General Tax Code is available to a small SARL/EURL meeting restrictive membership and turnover conditions, not to an SAS. Hybrid mismatch rules under EU ATAD are mandatory and may recharacterise cross-border payments or entities; no elective classifications are available outside the statutory framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: An established French SAS has no VAT registration threshold; French VAT compliance begins with the first taxable transaction. The small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA) for service activities, including remote desktop access and IoT telemetry software, applies only while annual turnover is ≤ EUR 36,600 (periodically adjusted by decree; a separate reduced threshold applies to certain regulated supplies). For intra-EU cross-border supplies of electronic services to consumers, a single Union-wide EUR 10,000 threshold applies before French VAT or VAT One-Stop-Shop (OSS) registration becomes mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured electronic invoicing for French domestic B2B transactions is phased in from 1 September 2026 (all businesses must be able to receive e-invoices; large and mid-sized suppliers must issue e-invoices) and from 1 September 2027 (small and medium-sized suppliers must issue e-invoices). Invoices must be issued in a DGFiP-approved structured format (Factur-X, UBL, CII or equivalent) and exchanged through an accredited dematerialisation platform (PDP) or the Public Invoice Portal (PPF). The transmission platform automatically forwards mandatory invoice data and VAT e-reporting data to DGFiP through secured APIs. No real-time fiscal clearance or Italian-style digital stamping is currently mandated; the model is an audit-oriented e-reporting pipeline with full interoperability requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For physical goods, exports from French/EU customs territory qualify for the French VAT exemption with right to input VAT deduction under Article 262-1 of the French General Tax Code, provided the goods are physically dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU and documentary proof of export is retained. For remote desktop access, screen sharing and IoT telemetry software supplied to a B2B customer established outside France, the supply is treated as outside the French VAT scope because the place of supply is the customer's jurisdiction under Article 259-1 of the French General Tax Code; proof of the customer's non-French business identity and VAT registration number is essential. B2C electronic services supplied to non-EU consumers are likewise outside the French VAT scope. No separate zero-rating certificate is required for these services; the important requirement is proper documentation of the customer's jurisdiction and, where relevant, the recipient's foreign VAT registration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DAU / ECS) validated by DGDDI evidencing the physical departure of the goods from the EU
Bill of Lading, CMR, air waybill or equivalent transport document showing outbound carriage to a non-EU destination
Inward remittance certificate or bank statement proving receipt of export proceeds and FX repatriation
Commercial invoice, sales agreement and any technical documentation supporting the transaction
Customer's foreign VAT identification number and, where applicable, EC Sales List evidence for intra-community supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating and out-of-scope service supplies are subject to intensive audit review by DGFiP and DGDDI. If the alleged export did not physically occur, the documentation is false or incomplete, or the customer's foreign VAT status is invalid, the VAT exemption or out-of-scope treatment is retrospectively withdrawn; all input VAT previously recovered or refunded is clawed back and the output VAT is reassessed for the full six-year limitation period. Penalties include an 80% bad-faith penalty for deliberate concealment, a 40% penalty for substantial omissions, and 30% or 10% for failures to file or declare, plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.20%. Criminal tax fraud under Article 1741 of the French General Tax Code can result in a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to five years. Under the Customs Code, fraudulent export declarations may lead to forfeiture of goods, a fine equal to one to three times the evaded duties and additional sanctions against the exporting company and its legal representatives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (member of the Eurosystem/ESCB) is the central monetary authority; exchange-control and foreign-investment statistical oversight is shared with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury, Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty), with operational AML/CFT supervision delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains no exchange-control regime; the euro is fully convertible and France observes IMF Article VIII obligations. Both current-account operations (software subscriptions, royalties, SaaS fees, trade in goods) and capital operations (equity injection, shareholder loans, dividend/profit remittance) are liberalized under TFEU Articles 63-66 without pre-authorization or quantitative limits for ISIC 6201 activity. Practical remittance hurdles are tax-driven only: dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders are subject to a 25% withholding tax under Article 119 bis 2 of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), reduced to 0% where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions (minimum 5% holding, two-year retention) are met, and treaty relief may further cap source taxation. Royalties and software service fees remitted to non-residents may attract withholding under Article 182 B CGI at 25% unless reduced by treaty or eliminated by the royalty directive for payments to EU beneficiaries. Transfer-pricing documentation under Article L. 13 AA CGI must support any cross-border intercompany payment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. France abolished export-proceeds surrender and conversion obligations in 1990; a French SAS may freely retain foreign currency in authorized foreign-currency accounts and may denominate invoices in any currency. The sole residual obligation is statistical reporting: every payment or credit between a French resident and a non-resident equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000 (single transaction or logically linked series) must be reported to the Banque de France under Regulation No. 2012-04 (as amended by Regulation No. 2023-01) for balance-of-payments statistics; transactions between EUR 10,000 and EUR 50,000 are aggregated and transmitted by the reporting bank quarterly. The enterprise must produce supporting invoices, contracts, and purpose codes upon demand. Cross-border cash or bearer transfers of EUR 10,000 or more require a customs declaration under Article L. 152-1 of the Code Monétaire et Financier. There is no mandatory conversion ratio and no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte de dépôt professionnel) for EUR collection, PSP settlement and treasury
Operational Account (Compte courant professionnel) for inbound/outbound payments and trade finance
Operational Account plus dedicated blocked deposit account (Capital Escrow Account) where investor-grade ring-fencing is required
Operational Account with multi-currency functionality for non-EUR disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for day-to-day treasury and PSP settlement through ACPR-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto (ACPR EMI licence, French IBAN) and Shine (Société Générale subsidiary), or EU-licensed EMIs passported into France (e.g., Revolut via its ACPR-branch status). Legal constraint: EMIs may issue electronic money and execute payment transactions but may not grant credit, open documentary credits, or act as statutory depositary for capital increase blocking certificates ('certificat de dépôt de fonds'), which under Articles L. 225-227 and L. 227-12 CGI/C. com. can only be issued by a licensed credit institution. Offshore digital EMIs without an ACPR single-passport or without registration as a payment agent under Article L. 521-3 Code Monétaire et Financier cannot lawfully provide payment services into France and must not receive French customer traffic; they may only act as white-label technical providers. For a French SAS with no minimum capital requirement, no legal capital-escrow account is mandated, but investors and auditors commonly require a Tier-1 bank account for substantial equity injections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is lawful under Article R. 561-12-1 of the Code Monétaire et Financier through (i) ANSSI-certified video identification, (ii) an eIDAS-qualified electronic signature, or (iii) a secure digital copy with dynamic verification. No statutory physical-appearance duty exists for standard corporate account opening. In practice, BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole/LCL, and BPCE require a real-time video interview with at least one authorized director or UBO and a French registered address for service of process; non-resident directors may appoint a French person as representative and may sign via notarized and apostilled powers of attorney. Enhanced due diligence applies where UBOs reside in non-EU or Financial Action Task Force high-risk jurisdictions, but full remote opening remains achievable for a standard-risk SAS in ISIC 6201.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: a chain of non-resident holding companies without filed French UBO declarations, or shell-company layers preventing identification of natural-person owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS extract containing the registered UBO declaration (Article L. 561-2-2 Code Monétaire et Financier), complete organizational chart of all intermediate entities, French share register and transfer ledger, passport copies and certified residential addresses of each natural-person UBO, and a funds-origin statement ratified by board minutes or an independent audit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-model mismatch: remote screen-share and unattended IoT telemetry software exhibiting high transaction velocity and small-ticket recurring micro-payments that can resemble mule or synthetic-payment behavior.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved business plan and SaaS revenue model, Stripe/Paddle settlement statements and payout history, standard end-user license and subscription contracts, privacy and data-protection register (RGPD/DPIA), ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certificates, and merchant category reporting evidencing genuine software sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP/sanctions exposure: any director or indirect shareholder is a politically exposed person or comes from a jurisdiction on French-EU sanctions or FATF monitoring lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions and PEP screening reports, formal PEP declaration forms, source-of-wealth memorandum with supporting bank and tax records, negative commercial-reputation due diligence prepared by counsel, and a written undertaking to maintain continuous screening for the life of the account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic disconnection in treasury flows: inbound capital injection followed by rapid outbound disbursements to foreign software developers or suppliers without a demonstrable commercial link.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement and capital-increase minutes, declaration of subscription and payment, depositary bank's sworn certificate of funds deposit, supplier contracts and pro-forma invoices, SWIFT purpose code explanations, and a 12-month cash-flow projection signed by the statutory auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital-only evidence and remote signatory risk: eIDAS signatures and video KYC perceived as insufficient for Tier-1 bank risk committees, particularly for non-resident directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office lease with French utility billing, French RCS and VAT certificates, notarized and apostilled powers of attorney for each authorized signatory, ANSSI-certified video-identification recordings, and certified translations of all corporate documents into French by a sworn translator (expert judiciaire).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity funding is executed by SEPA Credit Transfer (EUR, using the SAS's FR76 IBAN) or by SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR remitters (field 50K ordering customer, field 59 beneficiary account, field 70 purpose 'Apport en capital – augmentation de capital'), with the euro leg settled through TARGET2. No prior ministerial authorization applies to foreign investment in a French software company (ISIC 6201 is outside the strategic-sector decree of 31 December 2019 as amended). The bank requires the subscription deed, the shareholders' minutes approving the capital increase, the certificate of funds deposit, and source-of-funds evidence (investor bank statements, liquidation proof, or salary warrants). Any payment or series equal to or above EUR 50,000 is reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics; where the investor acquires at least 10% of voting rights, an inward FDI statistical declaration is filed with the Treasury/Banque de France OFI within 20 days of completion. Because the SAS has no minimum legal capital, no statutory blocking escrow is required, but if the parties contractually agree to hold funds pending inscription au RCS, the receiving bank may issue a blocked-deposit certificate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Euro disbursements within the EEA and SEPA zone are cleared via SEPA Credit Transfer on the T2 circuit, with SEPA Instant (limit EUR 100,000) available for real-time settlements; non-EEA or non-euro payments are routed via SWIFT MT103 (fields 32A, 57A, 71A, 72) through correspondent ACH systems (Fedwire/CHIPS, CHAPS, CIPS, ECS) with same-day or next-day value. Trade settlements involving documentary conditions use an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 and governed by UCP 600 with eUCP 2.0 addendum; MT707 amendments, MT752 payment authorizations, and Standby Letters of Credit under ISP 98 are available for IoT hardware and OEM component purchases. Every outbound transfer requires underlying pro-forma invoices or definitive contracts, and amounts exceeding EUR 50,000 trigger the bank's payment-reporting obligation plus an export declaration where physical goods cross borders. Stripe and Paddle, as the target payment rails, operate as licensed EU payment institutions and settle collected funds by SEPA Credit Transfer into the SAS's euro operational account, which remains fully compatible with the French clearing architecture and with the Banque de France reporting regime.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward (change à terme) with a French or EU supervised credit institution covering EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF exposures arising from SaaS subscriptions, MSP contracts, or supplier invoices; the hedge must mirror an underlying commercial exposure, as purely speculative treasury trading is outside the permitted scope for a non-financial corporate and may raise prudential and directors'-duty issues.
FX swap (swap de change) for rotating short-term USD or GBP positions where disbursements to non-EEA vendors are made in batches and where a single forward leg would create settlement-date mismatch.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) cash-settled in EUR on illiquid currencies (e.g., INR for Indian development subcontractors, TRY, NGN) where currency deliverability or convertibility restrictions in the counterparty jurisdiction prevent physical settlement; the NDF notion that must tie to a verifiable underlying invoice amount.

Cross-currency interest rate swap (basis swap) executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex where the SAS holds a EUR floating-rate loan and a USD-denominated contract portfolio; EMIR trade-reporting obligations apply and the clearing threshold for non-financial counterparties must be monitored.

FX option collar structures involving purchased options only (zero-cost collar or capped forward) through an EU-regulated market or a bank under an ISDA/CSA framework; writing naked options is prohibited for ordinary treasury risk-management purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting approving the financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders meeting (internal governance; minutes recorded in statutory minute book, no external filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after financial year-end (calendar-year SAS: by 30 June).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate sanction for late meeting, but annual accounts must still be approved and filed; prolonged delay may aggravate other filing penalties and expose directors to fines.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable_notes: Required for all SAS; minutes must be dated and signed and inserted in the register of decisions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (comptes annuels) with the Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval and in all cases no later than seven months after financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for calendar-year accounts).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Per-director fine up to EUR 1,500 for non-filing; court may order filing under judicial compulsion (astreinte); persistent non-filing may trigger RCS administrative strike-off (radiation).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, form 2065)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impot.gouv.fr
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year entities: second business day after 1 May, due to the time of online filing; non-calendar year-ends: within three months of fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 10% of assessed tax for late filing, increased to 40% for intentional non-filing and 80% in cases of fraudulent evasion; late-interest at 0.33% per month.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaration and payment of CVAE (ownership of business value-added tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due with the annual corporate tax return (same deadline as liasse fiscale) for entities having gross turnover above EUR 152,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration assessment: 10% penalty on the amount due plus monthly late interest; false declarations may attract 30% to 40% penalty depending on wilfulness.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payment of CFE (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Yearly tax roll; payment due by 15 December of the assessment year; instalment scheme available if annual CFE exceeds EUR 3,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: After 30-day deadline, 10% late-payment increase plus enforcement charges; continued non-payment can lead to attachment and recovery measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Update of RCS beneficial-owner declaration (Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) upon triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in shareholding or control resulting in a modification of the beneficial ownership data; no fixed annual date in France.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 7,500 for individuals and EUR 37,500 for legal entities; imprisonment of 6 months for deliberately false declarations; administrative strike-off in persistent cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) is compulsory for an SAS if, at fiscal year-end, the entity exceeds any two of the three thresholds: total balance sheet EUR 4,000,000, pre-tax turnover EUR 8,000,000, and permanent workforce 50 employees. Appointment may also be mandatory by court order at the request of shareholders representing at least 1/10 of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, PCG) for individual statutory accounts; IFRS is permitted (and mandatory where applicable) only for consolidated accounts of groups qualifying as public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a free-standing annual UBO confirmation statement. The RCS beneficial-owner declaration is filed at registration and must be re-filed whenever a shareholding transfer or control movement alters the identity, proportional interest, or nature of effective control; the re-filing is due within 30 days of the event. Companies are expected to perform an annual internal verification of this data, but the legal trigger remains the substantive change, not a calendar date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share movements and current members (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of shareholders' decisions and signed minutes (Minute book / Registre des décisions)
Registered office documentation, cards of directors, and record of control (Registre des biens, actions et titres)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 – USD 800 per year (domiciliation or legal representative address service in Paris or department of registration)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 12,000 per year for a small to mid-size SAS software company subject to statutory audit, depending on balance-sheet complexity and group structure
